en: Camille and Madeleine arrived one morning for the doll's funeral: they were delighted; Sophie and Paul were just as happy.
Come quickly, my friends, we've been waiting for you to make the doll's coffin.
But what shall we put her in?
I have an old toy box; nanny has covered it with pink cotton; it's very pretty; come and see.
The little girls ran to Madame de Réan's room, where the maid was finishing the pillow and the mattress that were to go in the box;

the children admired this charming coffin; they put the doll in it and, so that nobody would see the broken head, the melted feet and the broken arm, they covered her with a little pink taffeta quilt.
The box was placed on a stretcher that their mother had had made for them.
They all wanted to carry it; but that was impossible, since there was only room for two.

After a bit of pushing and arguing, it was decided that Sophie and Paul, the two smallest, would carry the stretcher, and that Camille and Madeleine would walk one behind and one in front, carrying a basket of flowers and leaves to throw on the grave.
When the procession reached Sophie's little garden, they put down on the ground the stretcher with the box containing the remains of the unfortunate doll.
The children began to dig the grave; they lowered the box into it, threw flowers and leaves on top, then the earth they had dug out; they quickly raked all around and planted two lilacs there.
To round off the celebration, they ran to the pond in the vegetable garden and filled their little watering cans to water the lilacs;
this led to new games and new laughter, because they splashed each other's legs, chased each other and ran away laughing and shouting.
There had never been a merrier funeral.
It's true that the dead one was an old doll, with no colour, no hair, no legs and no head, and that nobody loved her or missed her.
The day ended cheerfully; and when Camille and Madeleine left, they asked Paul and Sophie to break another doll so they could have another funeral as much fun as this one.
pt: A Camille e a Madeleine chegaram numa manhã para o enterro da boneca: estavam encantadas; a Sophie e o Paul não estavam menos contentes.
Venham depressa, amigas, estamos à vossa espera para fazer o caixão da boneca.
Mas onde é que a vamos pôr?
Tenho uma caixa velha de brinquedos; a ama forrou-a de percal cor-de-rosa; está muito bonita; venham ver.
As pequenas correram até ao quarto da senhora de Réan, onde a criada acabava a almofada e o colchão que se iam pôr na caixa;

as meninas admiraram aquele caixão encantador; puseram lá a boneca e, para que não se visse a cabeça partida, os pés derretidos e o braço partido, cobriram-na com uma pequena colcha de tafetá cor-de-rosa.
Puseram a caixa numa padiola que a mãe lhes tinha mandado fazer.
Queriam todos carregá-la; mas era impossível, porque só havia lugar para dois.

Depois de se empurrarem e discutirem um bocado, decidiu-se que a Sophie e o Paul, os dois mais pequenos, levariam a padiola, e que a Camille e a Madeleine iriam uma atrás e outra à frente, com um cesto de flores e folhas para deitar na sepultura.
Quando o cortejo chegou ao jardinzinho da Sophie, pousaram no chão a padiola com a caixa que continha os restos da desgraçada boneca.
As crianças puseram-se a cavar a cova; desceram a caixa, deitaram-lhe por cima flores e folhas, e depois a terra que tinham tirado; ancinharam depressa tudo à volta e plantaram lá dois lilases.
Para acabar a festa, correram ao tanque da horta e encheram os regadorzinhos para regar os lilases;
foi ocasião para novas brincadeiras e novas gargalhadas, porque molhavam as pernas uns aos outros, perseguiam-se e fugiam a rir e a gritar.
Nunca se tinha visto um enterro tão alegre.
É verdade que a morta era uma boneca velha, sem cor, sem cabelo, sem pernas e sem cabeça, e que ninguém gostava dela nem tinha pena dela.
O dia acabou alegremente; e, quando a Camille e a Madeleine se foram embora, pediram ao Paul e à Sophie que partissem outra boneca para poderem voltar a fazer um enterro tão divertido.
